source_locator.edition_or_translation: J. M. Ashmand translation from Proclus's Greek paraphrase; 1900 W. Foulsham & Co. new edition
source_locator.short_quote: Jupiter ... occupies the next two signs, Sagittarius and Pisces

condition.house_pair_source: Book I Chapter XX main text

normalized_rule: Ptolemy's Chapter XX assigns Jupiter the two houses Sagittarius and Pisces; the cited edition's footnote 49 orders Sagittarius as day and Pisces as night.
synthesis_notes: This is a source-specific house lookup, not a guaranteed personality or event outcome.
review_notes: Pairs with the existing Sun and Moon house rules. The main text supports Jupiter's two signs; the day/night order is an edition footnote/modern overlay, not silently attributed to Ptolemy. 'Domicile' remains normalized technique vocabulary.
transmission_notes: Chapter XX's main text assigns Jupiter's two signs. Footnote 49 says the day/night table is from Whalley and also found in modern writers; preserve that editorial/modern overlay separately from the Ptolemaic two-house assignment.
